title: Pushing images to ECR
idea: Amazon ECR is AWS's private registry for container images. ECS pulls your image from it when it starts your containers.
points: The registry address names your account and AWS Region, a geographic location.
Create the repository first; a push does not create one by default.
`aws ecr get-login-password` returns a token that lasts 12 hours.
The token has the same permissions as the IAM identity that requested it.

hero.title: An ECR image name, part by part

parts.label: Account ID
parts.note: Your AWS account ID, without hyphens. Every account has its own private registry.

parts.label: Fixed text
parts.note: Fixed text in standard private registry addresses.

parts.label: Region
parts.note: The Region where the repository lives, such as `us-east-2`. Login and push must use the same one.

parts.label: Domain
parts.note: Fixed text in most Regions. The slash ends the registry address and starts the repository name.

parts.label: Repository
parts.note: One repository per app. It holds every version of that app's image.

parts.label: Tag
parts.note: Names one version. Omit it and Docker assumes `latest`.

code.title: Create, log in, push
code.caption: Replace `<account-id>` and `<region>`. `bookstore-api:1.0` is the local image from chapter 9.

walk.text: Create the repository once. `IMMUTABLE` means a pushed tag such as `1.0` cannot be overwritten.
Log in: a pipe sends the token to `docker login`. The user name is `AWS`.
Tag the local image with the registry address. This only adds a name.
Push. Docker uploads only the layers ECR does not already have.

pitfalls: Keep the Region identical in `create-repository`, `docker login` and the image name.
Push a new tag for every change; an immutable repository rejects a second `1.0`.
ECS Fargate (next page) defaults to x86-64; build with `--platform linux/amd64` on Apple Silicon.

quiz.q: Which image name can `docker push` send to your ECR repository?
quiz.why: The name must start with the registry address, then the repository and tag. Without it, Docker aims at Docker Hub.

takeaway: Name the image with the registry address, log in, then push.
